name: print_file
description: Print the contents of a local file. Set line_numbers to prefix each line with its line number (cat -n style) when you need a file:line anchor, and use start_line/end_line to print only an inclusive line range so large files can be paged a window at a time. Numbered or ranged output is line-oriented and always ends with a newline even if the file does not; read the file with no options for a byte-exact copy.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the file.

line_numbers.description: Prefix each printed line with its line number in the file (cat -n style). Numbers are absolute file positions even when a range is requested. The number and tab prefix is not part of the file content, so strip it before reusing the text elsewhere — for example as patch_file's old_string. Defaults to false.

start_line.description: First line to print, 1-based and inclusive. Defaults to the first line of the file.

end_line.description: Last line to print, 1-based and inclusive. Defaults to the last line of the file. Must be greater than or equal to start_line.
